traceability.evidence:
Implementation, tests, and docs for Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS were found and align with the story’s requirements:
1. Core ESLint rules present - `src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts` - Declares ESLint rule `require-story-annotation` with meta: - `type: "problem"` - `docs.description`: "Require @story annotations on functions and auto-fix missing annotations where possible" - `schema` includes `scope` and `exportPriority` options with enums from shared constants. - Uses shared helper functions from `./helpers/require-story-helpers` and visitors from `./helpers/require-story-visitors`. - `create` hook wires `scope` and `exportPriority` into `shouldProcessNode` and `buildVisitors`: - `const scope = opts.scope || DEFAULT_SCOPE;` - `const exportPriority = opts.exportPriority || "all";` - Error message `missingStory` is explicit and actionable, including an example of a correct `@story` value. - `src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts` - Declares ESLint rule `require-req-annotation` with meta: - `type: "problem"`, `fixable: "code"` (though current usage sets `enableFix: false` in this rule). - `docs.description`: "Require @req annotations on function-like exports..." - `schema` includes the same `scope` and `exportPriority` semantics as `require-story-annotation`, using `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES`. - Imports and reuses the same `DEFAULT_SCOPE`, `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES`, and `shouldProcessNode` helpers as `require-story-annotation`. - `create` hook computes `scope` and `exportPriority` identically and uses `shouldCheck = shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)` for all supported node types. - For each function-like node (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) it calls `checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false })` when `shouldCheck` is true.
2. Shared function detection scope (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, Core Functionality) - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts` defines: ```ts export const DEFAULT_SCOPE: string[] = [ "FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction", ]; ``` - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts` re-exports `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and provides `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)` which: - Returns false if `node.type` is not in `scope`. - Applies `exportPriority` to include/exclude exported vs non-exported nodes via `isExportedNode`. - Both rules import the same `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and `shouldProcessNode`, so they operate on the same set of function-like constructs: - `FunctionDeclaration` - `FunctionExpression` - `MethodDefinition` - `TSDeclareFunction` - `TSMethodSignature` - Arrow functions are **not** in `DEFAULT_SCOPE`, so by default they are excluded from enforcement, satisfying the “Arrow functions are excluded by default” part of REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION.
3. Visitor implementation for require-story-annotation (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY) - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts` builds visitors for: - `FunctionDeclaration` → `buildFunctionDeclarationVisitor` → `handleFunctionDeclaration` - `FunctionExpression` → `buildFunctionExpressionVisitor` - `ArrowFunctionExpression` → `buildArrowFunctionVisitor` - `TSDeclareFunction` → `buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor` - `TSMethodSignature` → `buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor` - `MethodDefinition` → `buildMethodDefinitionVisitor` - Each handler checks `if (!options.shouldProcessNode(node)) return;`, ensuring that `scope` and `exportPriority` drive enforcement consistently. - Although an `ArrowFunctionExpression` visitor exists, `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and the documented schema for `scope` only include the 5 required types, and tests assert that unannotated arrow functions are allowed by default. This matches the story’s requirement that arrow functions are excluded by default.
4. JSDoc/comment parsing and shared strategy (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) - For `@story` (require-story-annotation): - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts` defines multiple detection helpers: - `jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node)` → uses `sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node)` and checks for `"@story"`. - `commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node)` → uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and scans for `"@story"`. - `leadingCommentsHasStory(node)` → inspects `node.leadingComments`. - `linesBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node, lookback)` in `require-story-io.ts` → scans preceding source lines. - `parentChainHasStory(sourceCode, node)` in `require-story-io.ts` → walks parent chain, checking comments. - `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node)` in `require-story-io.ts` → bounded text window search using `FALLBACK_WINDOW`. - `hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node)` orchestrates all these, wrapped in a `try {...} catch { /* noop */ }` to fail gracefully on malformed input. - For `@req` (require-req-annotation): - `src/utils/annotation-checker.ts` mirrors the strategy with `@req`-focused helpers: - `getJsdocComment`, `getLeadingComments`, `getCommentsBefore`, `combineComments`. - `commentContainsReq` to detect `"@req"` in comments. - `linesBeforeHasReq`, `parentChainHasReq`, and `fallbackTextBeforeHasReq` using shared `LOOKBACK_LINES` and `FALLBACK_WINDOW` from `require-story-io`. - `hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context, node)` combines heuristics (JSDoc, comments, line-based, parent-chain, fallback text), with `try/catch` to avoid throwing on malformed source. - Both rules therefore use a common, robust parsing/detection strategy for their respective annotations and include defensive error handling for malformed JSDoc or incomplete AST/source info, matching REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and the Error Handling acceptance criterion.
5. Annotation enforcement (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED) - `require-story-annotation` ultimately uses `reportMissing` / `reportMethod` from `require-story-helpers`: - `reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?)`: - Skips reporting if `hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node)` is true. - Resolves a name via `extractName` (with `(anonymous)` fallback) and reports `messageId: "missingStory"` with `data: { name, functionName: name }`. - Uses `createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget)` to provide an autofix and suggestion. - `reportMethod` similarly reports for methods, anchoring the error on the method name node. - `require-req-annotation` uses `checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false })` from `src/utils/annotation-checker.ts`: - Determines `hasReq` via `hasReqAnnotation(...)`. - If missing, calls `reportMissing(context, node, enableFix)` which: - Computes a function name via `getNodeName` and handles anonymous cases. - Reports `messageId: "missingReq"` with `data: { name, functionName: name }`. - Optionally attaches an autofix via `createMissingReqFix(node)` (currently disabled in `require-req-annotation` via `enableFix: false`, but fully implemented). - Together, when both rules are enabled, any in-scope function-like node is required to have both `@story` and `@req` annotations, fulfilling REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED and the core functionality acceptance criterion.
6. Configurable scope & export priority (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY) - Both rules share the same option schema and helper: - `meta.schema` in `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` define: - `scope`: array of strings with `enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE` and `uniqueItems: true`. - `exportPriority`: enum of `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES` i.e. `"all" | "exported" | "non-exported"`. - `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority = "all")` in `require-story-helpers.ts`: - Checks `node.type` against `scope`. - Uses `isExportedNode(node)` to determine export status by walking up to `ExportNamedDeclaration`/`ExportDefaultDeclaration`. - Applies `exportPriority` logic to include only exported, only non-exported, or all. - Tests explicitly validate these semantics for both rules: - `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts`: - `require-story-annotation with exportPriority option` block: - Valid: unexported function without `@story` when `exportPriority: "exported"`. - Invalid: exported function missing `@story` under `exportPriority: "exported"` with correct autofix. - `require-story-annotation with scope option` block: - Valid: arrow function ignored when `scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]`. - Invalid: function declaration missing annotation when scope is limited to `FunctionDeclaration`. - `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts`: - Multiple valid and invalid cases for `scope` and `exportPriority` ensuring the same semantics: - `FunctionExpression ignored when scope only includes FunctionDeclaration`. - `exported` vs `non-exported` behaviours for functions and methods under different `exportPriority` values. - This demonstrates that both rules support identical, coordinated semantics for `scope` and `exportPriority`, satisfying REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY.
7. Error location and messages (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, User Experience, Error Handling) - `require-story-annotation`: - `require-story-helpers.reportMissing` computes `nameNode` as `node.id` or `node.key` when they are `Identifier`s, falling back to `node`, ensuring the error is anchored as close as possible to the function name. - The message `missingStory` in `require-story-annotation.ts`: ```ts "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story that points to the implementing story file (for example, docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md)." ``` is clear, imperative, and includes a concrete example. - `require-req-annotation`: - `reportMissing` in `annotation-checker.ts` selects `nameNode` as `id`/`key` `Identifier` when present, else falls back to the node. - The `missingReq` message is defined in `require-req-annotation.ts`: ```ts "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') referencing the appropriate requirement from the story file." ``` which is similarly actionable and specific. - Tests confirm these behaviours: - `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts`: - For missing class method annotation, asserts `data: { name: "method", functionName: "method" }` and validates suggestions and outputs. - `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts`: - Multiple invalid cases assert `data: { name: "...", functionName: "..." }` for functions, methods, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, and anonymous expressions, showing consistent error context. - Error reporting helper functions use `try/catch` where reading source/JSDoc may fail, preventing crashes and satisfying the Error Handling acceptance criterion.
8. TypeScript support (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, Integration acceptance criterion) - Both rules explicitly target TypeScript function-like syntax: - Visitors for `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature` in `require-story-visitors.ts` and corresponding handlers in `require-req-annotation.ts`. - The helper logic (`resolveTargetNode`, `extractName`, `getNodeName`) is written to handle TypeScript node shapes. - Tests cover TS-specific cases for both rules: - `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts`: - Valid: TS declare function and TS method signature with `@story` annotations using `@typescript-eslint/parser`. - Invalid: TS declare function and TS method signature without `@story`, with autofix outputs. - `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts`: - Valid and invalid cases for `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature` with and without `@req`. - Uses `@typescript-eslint/parser` for TypeScript AST. - Documentation reinforces this: - `docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md` and `docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md` each list `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature` among supported node types and include TypeScript examples.
9. Documentation (Documentation acceptance criterion) - `docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md`: - References this story in header: `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Documents rule purpose, supported node types, options (`scope`, `exportPriority`), JSON schema, example configuration, and correct/incorrect examples including TypeScript. - `docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md`: - Similarly references this story. - Explains rule details, supported node types, options and their defaults, and provides extensive JS and TS examples (correct/incorrect) aligned with the implementation and tests. - The root `README.md` lists both rules and their documentation links and shows sample ESLint configuration with `"traceability/require-story-annotation": "error"`.
10. Tests and quality (Quality Standards, Tests acceptance part of DoD) - Rule tests exist and explicitly reference this story: - `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts` - Header includes `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`. - Uses `RuleTester` to cover: - Valid cases: different annotation forms (JSDoc, line comments), function declarations, expressions, class methods, TS declare functions, TS method signatures, and arrow functions (allowed by default). - Invalid cases: missing `@story` across all required node types, including TS nodes, with detailed expectations of errors and autofix outputs. - Explicit tests for `scope` and `exportPriority` options. - `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts` - Header includes `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and requirement references. - Uses `RuleTester` to cover: - Valid cases: `@req` alone and in combination with `@story`, across all required node types including TypeScript. - Invalid cases: missing `@req` under many scenarios, including anonymous and object-literal methods, with precise `data` assertions and option scenarios for `scope` and `exportPriority`. - Additional helper tests for error handling and edge cases: - `tests/rules/require-story-core.test.ts` – tests `createMethodFix` and `reportMethod` behaviours. - `tests/rules/require-story-core-edgecases.test.ts` – tests `createAddStoryFix` and `reportMissing` fallbacks, including missing JSDoc API branches. - `tests/rules/require-story-visitors-edgecases.test.ts` – ensures `buildVisitors` returns expected handlers and that handlers don’t throw on nodes lacking expected properties. - Jest configuration is present and annotated with this story: - `jest.config.js` has header `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and sets up `ts-jest`, test matching on `tests/**/*.test.ts`, and coverage settings. - Test execution via tools: - `npm test -- --ci --no-watchAll --runInBand --verbose` ran without any error output being reported by the tool wrapper (indicating no failing tests were observed during this invocation). - A targeted `npx jest tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts --runInBand --verbose --ci --no-watchAll` also completed without errors reported.
Given this evidence, the implementation of `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` fully satisfies the story’s acceptance criteria and technical requirements for function annotation validation.
